h1: The 8 Best Induction Cooktops Under $300 for Home Cooks and Pro Kitchens, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 induction cooktops under $300, from precise Nuwave burners to NSF-certified commercial units, scored on control and build.
summary: The Nuwave Precision Induction Cooktop Gold is the best induction cooktop under $300, with 96 temperature settings from 100 to 575 degrees F. The Nuwave Pro Chef and ChangBERT Professional Chef Edition are the NSF-certified commercial options, the Duxtop 8620BI adds a second burner, and the Duxtop 9610LS is the simple budget choice.
intro: Spending up to $300 on a countertop induction burner pushes you into a different set of choices than the budget end. You are no longer deciding whether induction works for you, you are deciding which of two upgrades matters: finer temperature control or commercial-grade construction. Few units deliver both, and the listings rarely say which one they chose.

The eight cooktops below split into precision models, commercial NSF-certified models and a two-burner double. Each is scored on how many temperature steps it offers, its build and certification, and what it asks of your kitchen. Missing numbers are flagged as missing.

products.name: Nuwave Precision Induction Cooktop Gold
products.verdict: 96 temperature settings from 100 to 575 degrees F in the Nuwave Gold line.
products.description:
The Nuwave Precision Gold gives you 96 temperature settings from 100 to 575 degrees F, in a countertop body. It is the finest-grained controller in this ranking.

Ninety-six steps means you are adjusting in roughly 5 degree increments, which is how professional chefs think about temperature. That range covers holding a sauce at 140 degrees F up to a hard sear at 550. It ranks first because no other unit here pairs a range this wide with steps this fine. The trade is that it does not carry an NSF mark, so it is not the choice for a licensed kitchen.

Buy it if you cook with specific temperatures in mind. Skip it if you need certified equipment.
products.idealFor: Cooks who work to exact temperatures.

products.name: Nuwave Pro Chef Induction Cooktop
products.verdict: An NSF-certified, commercial-grade Nuwave with precision temperature control.
products.description:
The Pro Chef is an NSF-certified, commercial-grade induction cooktop with precision temperature control. It sits in the $100 to $200 bracket.

NSF certification means the unit meets sanitation and construction standards for foodservice, which is the main reason to buy it over the Gold. It ranks second because the home cook gains little from the certificate, while the listing shares no temperature range or wattage, so the precision claim cannot be quantified.

Buy it if you serve food to the public or want a tough unit. Skip it if you only cook at home.
products.idealFor: Food trucks, pop-ups and small kitchens.
products.skipIf: Home cooking is all you do.

products.name: ChangBERT NSF Certified Professional Chef Edition Cooktop
products.verdict: NSF certified at 1800W, with a Schott glass surface and a large heating coil.
products.description:
The ChangBERT Professional Chef Edition runs at 1800W with a Schott glass surface and a large heating coil, and it carries an NSF certification for commercial use.

Schott is a well-known German glass-ceramic maker, and its glass resists thermal shock and scratching better than generic tops. That is the reason this model ranks above the plainer Duxtops. The large coil spreads heat across a wide pan. Against the Nuwave Pro Chef it lists real wattage but shares no temperature range.

Buy it if you want a durable surface and a certified build. Skip it if you want degree-level control.
products.idealFor: Busy kitchens that need a tough top.
products.skipIf: You want a precise degree readout.

products.name: Duxtop 8620BI/BTK35 Portable Induction Cooktop 2 Burner
products.verdict: Two burners sharing 1800W in a plug-in countertop body.
products.description:
The Duxtop 8620BI/BTK35 is a portable two-burner induction cooktop rated at 1800W total.

Two burners give you flexibility that no single-burner model can match, but 1800W is shared, so running both at once halves each. It ranks fourth because the extra burner is useful in a small kitchen while the listing offers no precision details. Duxtop is a mainstream brand with plenty of owner discussion.

Buy it if you need two cooking zones without wiring. Skip it if you want one powerful burner.
products.idealFor: Small kitchens needing an extra burner.
products.skipIf: You need full power on one burner.

products.name: Nuwave Gold Precision Induction Cooktop
products.verdict: An 8-inch heating coil with precision temperature control.
products.description:
This Nuwave Gold Precision is a portable burner with a large 8-inch heating coil and precision temperature control.

The bigger coil improves evenness in wide pans, and the Gold line is Nuwave's mid-tier. It ranks fifth because the listing is silent on the temperature range, unlike the 96-step Gold model above it.

Buy it if even heat in a skillet matters. Skip it if you want listed steps.
products.skipIf: You want a listed temperature range.

products.name: Duxtop Professional Portable Induction Cooktop P961LS
products.verdict: A professional-grade Duxtop burner in a silver and black finish.
products.description:
The Duxtop P961LS is the professional-grade version of the Duxtop countertop burner, in a silver and black finish.

The Professional label implies sturdier construction than the entry models, but the listing does not say what is different. It ranks sixth because there is no power figure, temperature range or certification to confirm the claim.

Buy it if you favour the Duxtop name and its look. Skip it if you want detailed specifications.
cons: Little to separate it from basic Duxtops

products.name: Duxtop 9610LS Portable Induction Cooktop
products.verdict: 1800W and 20 preset temperature settings, plain and reliable.
products.description:
The Duxtop 9610LS delivers 1800W with 20 preset temperature settings in a black countertop body.

It ranks seventh in this company because it is the basic model, and everything above offers finer control or a certification. For plain cooking it is excellent value, and its 20 presets are a clear step up from simple power dials.

Buy it if you do not need extras. Skip it if you want precision or a certified build.

products.name: Nuwave NSF-Certified Single Electric Burner
products.verdict: A portable NSF-certified single burner with precision control, in the $200 to $500 bracket.
products.description:
The Nuwave NSF-Certified Single Burner is a portable one-burner unit with precision temperature control and NSF certification.

It ranks last because it is the most expensive here and shares less detail than the Pro Chef, which also has NSF. The listing calls it a single electric burner, so confirm that the surface is induction before buying.

Buy it if you need the Nuwave NSF mark and nothing else will do. Skip it if the Pro Chef fits your needs.
cons: Listing calls it electric, not induction

whatMatters.detail: A controller with 96 steps lets you move in about 5 degree increments. Presets in 20 steps are coarser, and power-level dials are coarser still. For sauces and candy, finer steps cut the guesswork.
A low end near 100 degrees F supports warming and melting, while a top end of 575 allows hard searing. Listings that give no range leave you guessing. The Nuwave Gold lists 100 to 575.
NSF means the unit has been evaluated against foodservice sanitation and construction standards. Licensed kitchens may require it. For home cooking it is a bonus signal of good construction.

Glass takes thermal shock when a cold pan meets a hot top. Schott glass, as on the ChangBERT, is known for resisting it. A cracked top ends the life of a cooktop, so surface quality is worth attention.
A two-burner portable unit rated 1800W splits that total. That is fine for light cooking, but it halves each burner under full load. For serious searing, pick a single burner.

faq.q: Is NSF certification necessary at home?
faq.a: No. It matters if you sell food. At home it simply signals a higher construction standard.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Paying for certification you do not need, or ignoring cookware. Check the magnet test on your pans, and decide whether you need precision or commercial build.

faq.q: Is the Nuwave Gold worth it over a Duxtop?
faq.a: If you cook to specific temperatures, yes. Its 96 steps and 575 degree F ceiling beat the Duxtop's 20 presets. For general cooking the Duxtop is enough.

faq.q: Do I need a special outlet?
faq.a: A standard 120V outlet works, but avoid sharing the circuit with other heavy appliances. Doubles at 1800W total need a dedicated line.

faq.q: How do I care for the glass?
faq.a: Wipe it clean after it cools and avoid dragging pans. A ceramic cooktop cleaner handles burnt residue.
Yes, cast iron works well. Lift it rather than slide it to protect the glass.

finalTake: The Nuwave Precision Induction Cooktop Gold is the best induction cooktop under $300, with 96 temperature steps from 100 to 575 degrees F. If you cook professionally, the Nuwave Pro Chef or the ChangBERT Professional Chef Edition brings NSF certification. The Duxtop 8620BI adds a second zone, and the Duxtop 9610LS is the budget choice. Decide whether you need precision or certification first.
